About

I'm Ziad Mohamed Abdel Azim Abdel Salam, a third-year Networks student at WE Applied Technology School in Egypt. My passion lies in computer networking, cybersecurity, information technology, and digital infrastructure.


I've built foundations in routing, switching, network administration, cybersecurity fundamentals, Linux, Windows Server, and telecommunications infrastructure, and joined training programs, cybersecurity competitions, projects, and field training.

Projects

Featured · Prototype and development

Smart Consumer Network

IoT smart energy monitoring with a web dashboard. Role: Team Leader and Project Developer.

An electricity monitoring system designed to measure voltage and current, show readings on a dedicated web dashboard, and flag unusual conditions such as overload using configurable thresholds. A buzzer gives audible alerts, and a relay is planned for automatic power disconnection.


My contributions: led and coordinated the student team, defined the concept and objectives, took part in hardware planning and component choice, contributed to the dashboard and monitoring concept, troubleshot inconsistent current sensor readings, and documented the workflow.


Honest status: the hardware prototype works with an LCD and buzzer. The dashboard currently runs in demo mode with simulated data. Hardware-to-dashboard integration and relay cut-off are still in development and testing.


Hardware prototype (Normal and OVERLOAD), Proteus simulations, and dashboard screenshots with simulated data. Tap to enlarge.

Prototype

Arduino Electricity Monitoring Prototype

An experimental prototype that measures voltage and current and shows readings on an LCD. Components: Arduino Uno, ACS712 current sensor, voltage divider, 16x2 LCD, buzzer. Goals: read the sensor, measure voltage with a divider, display readings, explore calibration and stability, and test alerts. Circuit diagrams are in the gallery above.
